name: Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier
description: Trier, on Germany's Moselle River, was once called the "second Rome" and served as a capital of the Roman Empire around 300 AD. Its streets still hold a Roman bridge, city fortifications, an amphitheatre and enormous bathhouse ruins, along with the vast Aula Palatina, an imperial hall. Medieval landmarks, the Cathedral of St Peter and the Church of Our Lady, stand among them.
